description: Six-panel SEM micrograph composite (2 rows x 3 columns) of cold-rolled low-density steel strips, etched to reveal a two-phase structure. Top row is CR20%: (a) 0Cr, (b) 3Cr, (c) 6Cr; bottom row is CR20% + annealed: (d) 0Cr, (e) 3Cr, (f) 6Cr. Every panel carries a scale bar at the bottom right reading 20 um (panel (b) appears to read 30 um) and black orthogonal arrows labelled TD (horizontal, pointing left) and RD (vertical, pointing down). Yellow arrows in each panel mark the smooth grey gamma-austenite matrix and the dark-outlined delta-ferrite constituent. From 0Cr to 6Cr the delta-ferrite grows in both size and apparent area fraction: in (a)/(d) it appears as small, isolated, elongated particles, whereas in (c)/(f) it forms coarse, interconnected vermicular/rod-like networks; (b)/(e) are intermediate. The gamma matrix morphology stays broadly similar throughout. Comparing the two rows, the annealed panels (d-f) look essentially indistinguishable from the cold-rolled panels (a-c). The group argues that Cr addition raises the delta-ferrite content of the strips while 600 C annealing leaves the microstructure unchanged; no numeric phase fractions are printed on any panel.

CR20% + annealed 6Cr. SEM micrograph, 20 um scale bar; coarse interconnected delta-ferrite network similar to (c); TD/RD arrows present.

observations.observation: The figure is a six-panel SEM micrograph composite arranged as two rows of three panels, each showing an etched two-phase microstructure.
Every panel contains black orthogonal arrows labelled TD (pointing left) and RD (pointing down), defining transverse and rolling directions in the image plane.
Yellow arrows in each panel label two constituents: 'gamma' on the smooth grey matrix and 'delta' on the dark-outlined elongated phase.
Each panel has a scale bar at the bottom right; the text reads 20 um in (a), (c), (d), (e) and (f), while (b) appears to read 30 um.

The apparent size and area fraction of the dark-outlined delta-ferrite increases from 0Cr to 3Cr to 6Cr within each row: isolated small particles in (a)/(d), intermediate in (b)/(e), and coarse interconnected vermicular networks in (c)/(f).
The annealed panels (d-f) show no visually obvious morphological difference from the corresponding cold-rolled panels (a-c).
The caption assigns CR20%: (a) 0Cr, (b) 3Cr, (c) 6Cr; CR20% + annealed: (d) 0Cr, (e) 3Cr, (f) 6Cr.
The citing text states the volume fraction of delta-ferrite in the cold-rolled steel strips is 5%, 12% and 18%, respectively (for 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr).
The citing text states there is no significant change in the morphology and volume fraction of delta-ferrite in the strips after cold rolling.
The citing text states that the addition of Cr results in an increase of delta-ferrite fraction in the cold-rolled steel strips.
The citing text states that further annealing at 600 C has no significant effect on the microstructure of the cold-rolled steel strips.
No numeric phase fraction, composition or dimension values are printed on any panel; the only printed numeric labels are the scale-bar lengths.
